criteria.await_drain: A send waits, bounded by a caller deadline, for drain or buffer space instead of reporting saturation.
criteria.drain_event: Server sessions expose a drain event that resumes queued sends; the client keeps fail-fast because it has no drain hook.
criteria.fail_fast: A bounded adapter queue rejects a send with a domain error as soon as native reports saturation or the client buffer passes its cap.

backpressure.instructions: How should send backpressure reach the caller?

criteria.callback: Connect and accept register checked per-event handler callbacks; grouped session state threads through handler arguments.
criteria.reader: Connect and accept vend a stream::reader over ws::event for inbound flow, reusing stream close and cancel; sends take the session handle.
criteria.receive: One opaque session handle serves a dedicated ws::receive pull returning a ws::event variant alongside send and close operations.

surface.instructions: Which surface should carry WebSocket session events?

criteria.explicit_insecure: Connect accepts an explicit insecure flag, defaulting to secure, so loopback and self-signed testing stays possible.
criteria.no_wss: The client accepts ws:// only and rejects wss:// URLs; TLS termination stays outside Can.
criteria.verify_only: Wss always verifies against OS trust with no bypass, so self-signed servers only exercise the failure path.

tls_client.instructions: How should the client expose wss TLS?

criteria.accept_op: The route handler calls ws::accept on its request; the adapter upgrades through the stored native request and server, then dispatch emits no HTTP response.
criteria.marked_route: A route marker makes dispatch upgrade first and invoke the handler with a live session instead of a request.
criteria.separate_serve: A standalone ws::serve owns its own Bun.serve and hooks apart from the HTTP router.

upgrade.instructions: How should server upgrade meet the router?

state: Can compiles to TypeScript for pinned Bun 1.4.2 (bun-1.4.2-darwin-arm64-v1, revision 744846f844374847c902b5e7fd59b4342a51ef99). G-EVENT already selected pull with no new grammar: opaque stream::reader<T> and stream::writer with read_many, write_some, close and cancel; owner.ts keeps open to closing to closed with exactly one terminal publication. HTTP routes match method plus path exactly; handlers receive an http::request snapshot and their return value becomes the response through nativeResponse, while dispatch always abandons the request afterwards. Stream-marked routes skip the eager bounded pre-read via a routeKind peek. Pinned probes observe: server.upgrade succeeds after an await inside async fetch, and returns false on a plain GET so the exchange stays HTTP; server send returns queued bytes, -1 when saturated, 0 after close, and the server close call validates nothing (code 999 and a 200-character reason pass silently); client send before open throws InvalidStateError, client close rejects bad codes with InvalidAccessError and reasons over 123 UTF-8 bytes with SyntaxError; drain fires while a saturated queue flushes (2 drains across 40 saturated sends of 50 x 64 KiB, all 3276800 bytes delivered); binary arrives as Buffer on server hooks and on the client by default, or ArrayBuffer when the client sets binaryType; the server selects a subprotocol through upgrade response headers while Bun auto-selects the first offered protocol when the server stays silent; clean closes at codes 1000 and 1001 echo code and reason to both hooks with wasClean true, and an abrupt TCP drop surfaces as server code 1006 with an empty reason; wss against a self-signed server fails by default, and only the object second argument {tls:{rejectUnauthorized:false},protocols?} bypasses or offers protocols (no three-argument form); the constructor throws sync SyntaxError on garbage URLs and bad protocols but constructs http:// URLs that fail later; typed ws.data reaches every hook. Acceptance needs real client/server text and binary echo, two independent stateful sessions, an explicit protocol, graceful close and upgrade denial, plus rejection of bad close codes, overlong reasons, unsupported protocols and invalid addresses, and runtime coverage of oversized messages, saturated queues, slow handlers, callback failure, abrupt disconnect, close during pending sends and shutdown with live sessions. Hooks install once per server with typed session data selecting the owner; no automatic reconnect or replay; no raw event objects leak into Can; publish/subscribe stays excluded.
